correctness.rationale: The invariant axis reduces to z'=q(z); positivity above z₀ and q(z)∼cz² give the stated integral for the maximal time. The reciprocal height extends analytically at s=T−t=0 through w_s=c−bw+aw² and w(0)=0. The variational height component receives transverse forcing but cannot affect u,v. In s, v=−u_s and the scalar equation is u_ss+z u_s+u=0. The analytic constant-term-one mode has no linear term, quadratic coefficient −c/[2(c+1)], and nonzero recursion denominators n(n−1+1/c) for n≥1. Reduction of order produces an integrand s^(−1/c)(1+O(s)), after scaling; integrating from zero for c>1 removes the constant component, integrating at c=1 gives log s, and for c<1 the leading power dominates any constant or lower-order resonance logarithm. Differentiating the reduction-of-order formula verifies the negative velocity normalization. The ratio |v_f|/z is asymptotic to c s^(1−1/c). For c>1, in the stated tube z'≥κz² and at |y|/z^p=Y the derivative is bounded above by Xz^(−p)+(1−pκ)Yz<0 for large Z. Integrating |y|dt in increasing z bounds the drift in x by Y z₀^(p−1)/[κ(1−p)]<X/2, closing all boundaries. The time bound follows by integrating 1/z², and ODE continuation rules out a bounded finite endpoint. In the tube the uniform estimate Q=z'=cz²[1+O(1/z)] yields the pole rate and the linear scalar identity along each trajectory for y z^(−1/c), with coefficient O(z⁻²) and forcing O(z^(−2−1/c)). Both are integrable and yield a finite limit C. Integrating dx/dz=y/Q gives x_∞−x=C z^(1/c−1)/(c−1)+o(z^(1/c−1)), also when C=0. The positive integrating-factor quotient gives C>0 for y₀>X/(κz₀); this is a nonempty open subregion for large z₀. Independently verified the explicit example's inequality margins at Z=10000: 49984999, 1249999/1000, and drift bound 4/15<1/2; for larger z the appropriately normalized error terms are decreasing. The other specialization has discriminant −79/40000 and exponent −9.
residual_risks: The attached numerical script was not executed and is not needed for the quantified proof. The c≤1 trichotomy is linearized only. The open tube is a sufficient subset for c>1, not a global basin characterization.

value.rationale: Axial Riccati escape alone would be an elementary observation. In this previously studied flow the explicit high-height open set and nonlinear amplitudes give a substantive complementary description to selected bounded simulations, and the linear trichotomy distinguishes transverse position from velocity or their ratio to height. The result is useful for interpreting which initial conditions can be simulated globally and where a linear pole response does not by itself prove a nonlinear statement.
residual_risks: No claim about the full escape basin, stability outside the stated regime, or transience of the published bounded numerical orbit.
